assassin: Call the name of another character. When the killed character is called to take its turn, it must remain silent and skip its entire turn for this round without revealing its card.
witch: Gather resources, then call the name of another character to bewitch; your turn is put on hold and you cannot build. When the bewitched character is called, its owner gathers resources and their turn immediately ends (no build, no character ability). You then resume your turn as if you were playing the bewitched character: you use that character's abilities and build limit, with YOUR hand, YOUR gold, and YOUR city. If the bewitched character is not in play this round, you do not resume.
magistrate: Assign three warrant markers facedown to three different characters; one is the signed warrant, the target. If the targeted player pays to build a district during their turn, you may reveal the warrant and confiscate that district, building it in your city for free. The confiscated district counts toward the target's building limit and the target gets their gold back. You may confiscate only the first district the target pays to build, and only if you do not already have an identical district.
thief: Call the name of another character. When a player reveals that character to take its turn, you immediately take all of that player's gold. You cannot rob a rank 1 character, the killed character, or the bewitched character.
spy: Choose another player and name a district type. Look at that player's hand. For each card of the named type, take 1 gold from that player and gain 1 card from the deck. If the player has fewer gold than matching cards, take all their gold and still gain a card per matching card.
blackmailer: Assign two threat markers facedown to two different characters; one shows the flowered lace and is the target. When a threatened player is called, they must gather resources, then resolve the threat: they may bribe you by giving half their gold rounded down (a player with 1 gold gives 0), removing their marker; or refuse. If they refuse you may reveal their marker; revealing the flowered lace takes all their gold. A threatened player must resolve the threat before using abilities or building. You cannot threaten a rank 1 character, the killed character, or the bewitched character.
magician: Choose one: exchange your entire hand with another player's hand (if you have zero cards you simply take theirs), or discard any number of cards from your hand to the bottom of the deck and draw an equal number.
wizard: Look at another player's hand and choose one card. Either pay to build it immediately (it does not count toward your building limit) or add it to your hand. During this turn you may build districts identical to districts already in your city.
seer: Take a card at random from each other player's hand and add them to your hand, then give one card from your hand to each player you took from. A player with no cards is skipped. Your building limit this turn is two.
king: Gain 1 gold per noble district in your city. At some point during your turn you must take the crown. If killed, at end of round reveal the King and take the crown as heir. If bewitched, you still take the crown.
emperor: Gain 1 gold per noble district in your city. You must take the crown from its holder and give it to a different player, not yourself, then take either 1 gold or 1 random card from that player's stash or hand. If killed, at end of round take the crown and pass it to a different player, taking nothing. Not usable in 2-player games.
patrician: Gain 1 CARD per noble district in your city. At some point during your turn you must take the crown. If killed, at end of round reveal the Patrician and take the crown as heir. If bewitched, you still take the crown.
bishop: Gain 1 gold per religious district in your city. During this round the rank 8 character cannot use its ability on your districts. If killed, rank 8 may target you; if bewitched, rank 8 cannot target the Witch's districts but can target the Bishop's.
abbot: Gain either 1 gold or 1 card per religious district in your city, in any combination you declare before taking. If at any point during your turn you are not the richest player, the richest player must give you 1 gold; on a tie you choose which tied player pays, and if you are among the tied you receive nothing.
cardinal: Gain 1 CARD per religious district in your city. When you build a district and lack the gold, you may take the shortfall from one player, giving that player one card from your hand per gold taken. The player cannot refuse and you cannot take more than needed.
merchant: Gain 1 gold per trade district in your city, plus 1 extra gold. Usable regardless of which resource you gathered this turn.
alchemist: At the end of your turn, take back all the gold you paid to build districts this turn, but not gold paid for other reasons such as the Smithy or the Tax Collector. You can only build what you could afford at the time.
trader: Gain 1 gold per trade district in your city. Trade districts do not count toward your building limit this turn, so you may build any number of them in addition to your limit.
architect: Gain two extra cards, usable regardless of which resource you gathered this turn. Your building limit this turn is three.
navigator: Gain either four gold or four cards, usable regardless of which resource you gathered this turn. You cannot build any districts this turn, not even districts that would not count toward your building limit.
scholar: Draw seven cards from the deck and choose one to add to your hand; shuffle the other six back into the deck. Your building limit this turn is two.
warlord: Gain 1 gold per military district in your city. You may destroy one district of your choice, yours or a rival's, by paying one fewer gold than its cost. You cannot destroy a district in a completed city. Destroyed districts go to the bottom of the deck.
diplomat: Gain 1 gold per military district in your city. Exchange one district in another player's city for one in yours, paying the difference if theirs costs more. You cannot take from a completed city, nor take a district identical to one you already have, and the district you give must not be identical to one they already have.
marshal: Gain 1 gold per military district in your city. Seize one district costing three or less from another player's city by paying its owner gold equal to its cost. You cannot seize from a completed city, nor seize a district identical to one you already have.
artist: Beautify up to two of your districts by placing one gold from your stash on each. A beautified district's cost is permanently increased by one, so it scores one more point and costs one more to destroy. Each district can be beautified only once.
queen: If you are sitting next to the player who revealed the rank 4 character, gain three gold. If that character is next to you but was killed, gain three gold when the card is revealed at end of round. Not usable with fewer than five players.
tax-collector: While the Tax Collector is in the game, immediately after any player builds a district they place one gold from their stash on the Tax Collector's token, even if they did not pay to build it. A player with no gold left after building pays nothing, and the Tax Collector pays no tax. At any time during your turn you may take all gold from the token. The tax is charged even in rounds where the Tax Collector is not in play, and leftover gold carries over. In 2-3 player games a player holding the Tax Collector still pays tax for their other character.
gold-mine: When you choose gold while gathering resources, take 1 extra gold.
library: When you choose to draw cards while gathering resources, keep both cards you drew.
observatory: When you choose to draw cards while gathering resources, draw three and keep one.
school-of-magic: During resource gathering it counts as a district of any one type you choose. As the King it can count as noble, and so on.
park: If you have no cards in hand at the end of your turn, draw two cards.
poor-house: If you have no gold at the end of your turn, take one gold from the bank.
factory: Your other unique districts cost one less gold to build.
quarry: You may build a district identical to one already in your city. Only one duplicate may exist in your city at a time. You cannot use the Magistrate, Diplomat, or Marshal to acquire an identical district.
framework: You may build any district by destroying the Framework instead of paying its cost. The Magistrate cannot confiscate a district built by destroying the Framework.
necropolis: Instead of paying the Necropolis's cost, you may destroy any one district in your city. The Magistrate cannot confiscate a Necropolis built without paying its cost.
stables: Building the Stables does not count toward your building limit this turn, so you may build another district afterward. If confiscated by the Magistrate, you may still build another district.
monument: You cannot build the Monument if your city already has five or more districts. It counts as two districts when counting districts at end of game.
secret-vault: The Secret Vault cannot be built. Score 3 extra points at end of game if it is still in your hand.
thieves-den: You may pay for the Thieves' Den partly or fully with cards from your hand at 1 card = 1 gold. If confiscated by the Magistrate, you receive back only gold spent, not cards.
keep: The Warlord cannot destroy the Keep.
great-wall: The Warlord pays one extra gold to destroy your districts; the Diplomat pays one extra gold to exchange them. The Diplomat does not apply the Great Wall's effect to the district he is exchanging from his own city.
armory: On your turn you may destroy the Armory to destroy any one other player's district. A district in a completed city cannot be destroyed.
basilica: At end of game score 1 extra point for each district of odd cost in your city.
capitol: At end of game, if you have at least three districts of one type, score 3 extra points. This can score only once.
dragon-gate: At end of game score 2 extra points.
imperial-treasury: At end of game score 1 point for each gold in your stash.
ivory-tower: If the Ivory Tower is the only unique district in your city at end of game, score 5 extra points. If the Haunted Quarter is also present and counted as a non-unique type, the Ivory Tower still scores.
map-room: At end of game score 1 point for each card in your hand.
statue: If you hold the crown at end of game, score 5 extra points.
wishing-well: At end of game score 1 extra point for each unique district in your city.
haunted-quarter: At final scoring, count it as a district of any one type you choose. If you choose a type other than unique, it no longer counts as unique for other scoring.
museum: Once per turn, place a card from your hand under the Museum. At end of game score 1 point per card under it. If the Museum is exchanged or seized the cards stay with it; if destroyed the cards are discarded to the bottom of the deck.
laboratory: Once per turn you may discard one card from your hand to take 2 gold.
smithy: Once per turn you may pay 2 gold to draw 3 cards from the deck.
theatre: At the start of the round you may exchange your character card for a random character card from another player. You choose the player blindly. In 2-3 player games you choose which of your two characters to give and randomly take one of your opponent's.
